name: headrush-core
description: HeadRush Core / Prime Remote Editor. An object tree, not a REST API: every node has properties you GET and PUT, and typed methods you POST positional arguments to. A rig is not a resource - it is whatever is currently loaded, so building one means making a new rig, setting properties on the live patch, and saving. Captured against a paired Core (AZ0X Web Server 0.6.2); the read path and the object-method call shape were exercised directly, and every method signature here is the device's own x-methods declaration.

notes.values: Continuous parameters are 0-1 on the wire. The minimum/maximum the device publishes is the display range; sending 65 for a Bass knob that reads 0-100 pegs it. See rigsmith.protocol.calibrate.
notes.chain: Chain.ModuleType1..14 are the fourteen slots, each an index into the module table at /Evil/API/Blocks ModuleTypes. 0 is an empty slot.
notes.instances: Every block type exists twice - 'Amp' and 'Amp 2' - so a rig can hold two. The second is addressed at /Evil/Engine/Patch/<Block>_2.
notes.pairing: POST /api/auth is not listed here. Pairing earns the right to use this map, so it cannot be one of its operations.

subtree.description: Everything at and under a node: metadata, methods and live values.

object_meta.description: One node's schema - parameter types, ranges and option lists.

set_properties.description: Set one or more live values on a node. Continuous values are 0-1.

new_rig.description: Make and load a new empty rig. Prompts on the device if the loaded rig is dirty; new_rig_confirm answers that prompt.

set_chain.description: Set ModuleType1..14 to place blocks in slots.

set_module_type.description: Put a module in a slot. Slot is 1-14; module_type indexes the module table.

serialize_block.description: A block's whole state as a JSON string, in display units. Read-only, and the cheapest way to snapshot a block before changing it.

deserialize_block.description: Restore a block from a serializeBlock string.

module_table.description: ModuleTypes: the index the chain slots refer to.

write_rig.description: Build a rig on the device. There is no create-then-populate resource here: makeNewRig loads a blank rig, the chain and block properties are set on whatever is loaded, and saveRigAs commits it under a name.
